name: International Rescue Committee
mission: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic well being, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is at work in over 40 countries and 26 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities.
theoryOfChange: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) utilizes an interactive Outcomes and Evidence Framework (iOEF) which includes explicit Theories of Change (ToC) to guide program design and measure impact. This framework delivers key information on outcomes related to health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power through theories of change that demonstrate how to achieve these outcomes, evidence for which interventions work, and guidance on how to measure progress. The IRC systematically uses theories of change in all new project designs, defining a theory of change as a set of evidence-based causal hypotheses that articulate the necessary steps required to achieve a specific outcome. Additionally, the IRC has a 'CRRD Program Quality Framework' called IMPACT, which defines program quality through six interconnected principles and supports the goals of their broader 'Strategy100'. The Strategy100 itself serves as a strategic plan that provides a 'north star' for their programs, research, and advocacy, focusing on five key outcome areas.

strengths_deep_dive: The International Rescue Committee demonstrates institutional strength through its massive reach and operational efficiency. In FY2024, it directed a vast majority of its resources to direct aid, recording a <cite id="3">87.7% program expense ratio</cite>. Independent evaluators consistently recognize this governance, resulting in a <cite id="1">97/100 overall Charity Navigator score</cite> and full compliance with <cite id="1">all 20 BBB accountability standards</cite>.

The organization's field operations produce measurable outcomes across global crisis zones. Its 2024 impact reports document over <cite id="4">24 million vaccine doses delivered</cite> and <cite id="4">1,140,000 children enrolled in foundational learning</cite>. These direct humanitarian outputs reflect the charity's capacity to deploy capital effectively in complex environments.
rich_narrative.summary: Founded in <cite id="10">1933</cite>, the International Rescue Committee provides vital emergency relief and long-term recovery support to individuals displaced by conflict and disaster worldwide. In FY2024, the organization managed <cite id="3">$1,341,268,864 in revenue</cite> to fuel its large-scale humanitarian programs. The organization demonstrates exceptional spending efficiency, with a <cite id="3">87.7% program expense ratio</cite> that easily exceeds the <cite id="1">75% industry standard</cite>. Based on its scored filings, the charity achieved an 88% program ratio, demonstrating clear alignment with donor expectations. The organization maintains an <cite id="1">overall score of 97.0/100 from Charity Navigator</cite>, backed by a <cite id="1">100/100 score in Leadership</cite> and a <cite id="1">Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid</cite>. While its massive international operations involve higher per-beneficiary costs, the charity proves its ability to deliver impact at scale.
